title: Insisting on Righteousness
note: Of the three those sages teach, righteousness alone, unlike wealth and pleasure, yields this life, the next and release. So this chapter says it is stronger than they are, and that also explains its place.

couplets.plain: Righteousness brings distinction and it brings wealth. What gain could be greater for a living being?
couplets.pm: It gives release, and it gives wealth such as heaven. So what gain is greater than righteousness? Release is called distinction because it is the best of all attainments. “Living being” here means human life, since only that can reach these two. No good is greater than righteousness.
couplets.note: சிறப்பு is literally distinction. He reads it as release, and wealth as heaven and the like.

links.quote: What gain could be greater for a living being?
links.reason: Asks what could pay better than the one thing that brings both distinction and wealth.

couplets.plain: There is no gain greater than righteousness, and no ruin greater than forgetting it.
couplets.pm: There is no gain greater than doing righteousness, and no ruin greater than forgetting it through delusion. The first half repeats the last couplet so as to say what ruin follows when it isn’t done.

links.quote: no ruin greater than forgetting it

couplets.plain: However you can, never stopping, do righteous deeds everywhere they can be done.
couplets.pm: By whatever means you have, do righteous deeds without a break, through every channel open to them. Household righteousness is done as your wealth allows, and ascetic righteousness as your body allows. The channels are mind, speech and body, and their deeds are good thoughts, good words and good acts.

links.reason: Asks for righteous deeds without pause, as far as one can and wherever they can be done.

couplets.plain: To be without stain in your mind is all of righteousness. Everything else is noise.
couplets.pm: Be free of fault in your mind: that much alone is righteousness. The fault is thinking evil. Words and outward show aren’t righteousness but noise, done so that others will notice. If the mind is stained, what is done by speech and body brings nothing.

links.reason: Reduces the whole of righteousness to one thing, a mind without stain.

links.quote: To be without stain in your mind
links.reason: Asks for a mind without stain and writes off all else as noise.

couplets.plain: Envy, craving, anger and harsh words: righteousness is a life free of these four.
couplets.pm: Envy of what others gain, craving for the objects of the senses, the anger towards others that these cause and the harsh words that anger brings: righteousness is what goes on without a break, free of these four. Whatever is mixed with them isn’t righteousness. This couplet and the last tell its nature.

links.quote: righteousness is a life free of these four
links.reason: Defines righteousness as the shunning of four named faults.
First of the four that righteousness must be free of.
அவா is the wanting itself, second on the list.
Third of the four, set beside envy and craving.

couplets.plain: Don’t say “I’ll see to it some other day.” Practise righteousness, for it is the companion that doesn’t die when you die.
couplets.pm: Don’t think “I am young, and I will do it when I am dying.” Practise righteousness daily. When life leaves this body it is the undying companion, because it stays with the soul and goes on into the next body. So do it while this passing body lasts.

links.quote: the companion that doesn’t die when you die
links.reason: Calls it the companion that does not die when you die.

links.quote: I’ll see to it some other day

couplets.plain: You needn’t be told what the way of righteousness is. See it between the one who bears the palanquin and the one who rides in it.
couplets.pm: The fruit of righteousness needn’t be taught from scripture. You can see it for yourself between the one who carries the palanquin and the one who rides in it. This is proof by sight, and it makes clear that righteousness is the undying companion.
couplets.note: The Tamil can also mean: don’t say that the gap between carrier and rider is the way of righteousness. He takes it as the plain reading does, except that he reads ஆறு as fruit, not way.
couplets.sensitive: implies a labourer's low station is earned by past wrongs

links.quote: the one who bears the palanquin and the one who rides in it

couplets.plain: If you do good and let no day fall away, that is a stone that blocks the road of your living days.
couplets.pm: If you do good and let no day pass idle, that deed is the stone that blocks the road by which days joined to a body come. While the two kinds of deeds born of the five faults remain, the soul stays in a body to taste their fruits, pleasure and pain. All those days are “living days”. So righteousness brings release.

couplets.plain: Only what comes from righteousness is joy. All else is outside it, and brings no praise.
couplets.pm: Only what comes with household righteousness is pleasure, meaning the enjoyment of desire. What comes without it, even if it is pleasure, belongs with pain, and has no praise either. Sins such as wanting another man’s wife seem pleasant for a moment and then turn to pain. Only those who do righteousness gain joy in this life, and praise.

links.quote: Only what comes from righteousness is joy
links.reason: Allows no joy but the one that comes of it, and puts all the rest outside and without praise.

couplets.plain: What you ought to do is righteousness. What you ought to avoid is whatever brings blame.
couplets.pm: What a person should do is good deeds. What a person should give up is evil deeds. Blame here stands for what is blamed. This lays down what to do and what to leave undone.

links.quote: What you ought to do is righteousness
links.reason: Gives the whole rule of action: do what is righteous and avoid what brings blame.

ideaLinks.reason: Righteousness brings wealth along with distinction.

ideaLinks.quote: To be without stain in your mind is all of righteousness
ideaLinks.reason: All righteousness is held in a mind without stain, and the rest is noise.

ideaLinks.remove: The Tamil says only that a stone blocks the road of living days. Further births and release are his reading, not its words.
